title: California tax threat
summary: A letter threatened San Quentin if he and Finegan came to California.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I don't know. I can't know what they really feel. You know, there is one thing that I did fail to mention and I think I should, since this is a historical thing, around 1959 or so, when I should really have gone and taken a fly on the west coast on film, there came a letter from California Tax Department to the effect that if either of these two guys show up in California and we know about it, the first thing we'll do is put them in San Quentin.
Yes. And I think that letter might still be with (inaudible).
I told him to keep it; whether he did or not I don't know. That kept me from going there.
Why, between Uncle Sam and the California State Government, why did they take such an aggressive and hostile tact towards you and Bill?
Because I think it was assumed we were quite successful, for one thing--
(Side B of Tape 5 ends at this point. Transcript will continue with Tape 6.)
The other thing is that it was a typical, squareish reaction to anyone who is involved in art, especially in show business; they assumed they're essentially irresponsible brats.
